Yes, Monzo offers arranged overdrafts in the UK for eligible personal current account holders aged 18 and over.   
Monzo

Interest Rates & Costs

Instead of daily flat fees, Monzo charges an Effective Annual Rate (EAR) based on your credit score and financial history:   
Monzo

Rates: 19%, 29%, or 39% EAR (variable). Most customers are offered the representative rate of 39% EAR.   
Monzo
+ 1

Limits: Up to £2,000 (or up to £3,000 for select customers), depending on what Monzo assesses you can safely afford.   
Monzo

No Hidden Fees: There are no extra setup fees, late fees, or charges for declined payments if you hit your limit.   
Monzo

Representative Example:If you borrow £1,200 for 30 days at 39.0% EAR (variable), it will cost you £32.94 in interest. (Note: Interest is calculated daily on your overdrawn balance and collected on the 1st of each month).   
Monzo
+ 1

Eligibility & How It Works

Credit Checks: Monzo checks your eligibility using your account data alongside credit reference agencies (TransUnion, Experian, and Equifax). Checking your eligibility in the app uses a soft search and won't affect your credit score.   
Monzo
+ 1

In-App Control: If eligible, you can switch your overdraft on, adjust your limit, or cancel it anytime directly from your profile settings in the Monzo app.   
Monzo

Unarranged Overdrafts: If you don't have an arranged overdraft—or try to spend past your limit—Monzo will normally decline the transaction for free. If an offline payment (like a train ticket or in-flight purchase) pushes you into an unarranged overdraft, Monzo won't charge extra fees, though you should top up the balance quickly as it can negatively impact your credit file.

Tip: Because 39% EAR is relatively steep compared to some UK competitors (like Starling or First Direct, which offer lower rates or small interest-free buffers), Monzo's overdraft is best kept as a short-term emergency buffer rather than for ongoing borrowing.
